title: tw CLI --json output
description: The shape of every tailworks command's --json output (docs/cli-json.md). $defs are named after the command ('deploy', 'tenant ls'); 'dev.event', 'deploy.event', 'logs.record' and 'logs.line' are NDJSON lines; 'error' is the error line on stderr. Objects may gain properties; the required ones and every listed type are stable. cmd/tw TestAgentEval and TestCLIJSONContract check real output against this file.

policy.description: tw policy [dir]: everything the app needs in the tailnet policy, before it is deployed (exits acl_denied, as an error, when a checked part is missing)

checked.description: false when mgmt can't read the tailnet policy (no Policy File › Read scope)

preflight.description: the dry-run preflight, as in deploy

callerGrant.description: the grant that lets tailnet members call the app (not checked)

serviceCallerGrant.description: for an app behind a Tailscale Service: the grant to its svc: name; callers' app capabilities go on this grant (not checked)

snippet.description: everything to add to the policy, in one block

applied.description: --apply: what mgmt wrote to the tailnet policy (changed, added, manual, oldETag, newETag, and the preflight after it)

timings.description: wall times in milliseconds, by phase

nodeBudget.description: tailnet nodes (docs/limits.md#tailnet-node-budget): what an app costs (tw policy and tw deploy), the tenant's live nodes, and warnings when that count is within 80% of the tenant's maxObjects or of its hosts' node capacity. Every node is a device on the tailnet

app.description: tw policy and tw deploy: the app's cost, from its tailworks.jsonc

public.description: public-ingress nodes: one per copy of an app with public routes

fixed.description: workload + public: the nodes the deploy itself joins

perObjectClasses.description: Durable Object classes whose every object gets a node of its own

sharedClasses.description: classes with "node": false: their objects add no node

tenant.description: the tenant's live nodes, by what they are; absent when mgmt couldn't be asked

objects.description: Durable Objects with a node of their own, sub-agents included

pool.description: pre-joined pool nodes waiting for a new object

maxObjects.description: the tenant's quota of live nodes (tw tenant set --max-objects)

capacity.description: the live hosts' node capacity (tw-hostd -capacity-nodes) and the nodes they run for every tenant; absent when the caller may not list hosts

code.description: a code from docs/errors.md; act on it, not on message

hint.description: what to do next: the fix lines joined with newlines, a usage line, or where to read about the code

error.description: one line on stderr when a command fails (exit 1, or 2 for an unknown command); stdout is then empty

object.description: one object: a workload node or a Durable Object instance with its own node

parent.description: the object that spawned this one

verified.description: every chain's hashes and host signatures verify

truncated.description: bare tw audit stopped at -n; older records exist (tw audit --all)

agentPlan.description: what tw agent setup or remove did, or would do

applied.description: false with --dry-run or when nothing needed doing

secret.description: a secret's metadata; no command returns a value

mcp.description: tw mcp --config (and tw mcp --json, or tw mcp on a terminal): how to register tailworks' MCP server (tw mcp with stdin a pipe is the MCP stdio protocol itself)

url.description: mgmt's /mcp, for an agent on a tailnet machine

stdio.description: the command an agent runs (the stdio bridge)

tools.description: the tools this caller may call

commands.description: by agent ID (claude, codex, cursor, gemini, opencode): the command, or the config JSON; json: the generic mcpServers entry

agents.description: how to register the server with each supported agent, the ones installed here first

command.description: a shell command that registers it (absent when the agent takes config instead)

detected.description: the agent looks installed on this machine

grant.description: the github.com/rosskukulinski/tailworks/cap/mcp grant that adds the missing tools

telemetry.description: tw telemetry [show], set and rm: the tenant's OTLP export (header values are never shown; rm prints only tenantID)

updateCheck.description: the once-a-day update check (api.github.com, after interactive commands other than tw dev and tw init) is on: a release build without CI or TW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK set

updateAvailable.description: --check: latest is newer than this tailworks (false for a development build)

upgrade.description: --check, when updateAvailable: the command that installs it

securityRelease.description: --check: the latest release's notes have a Security section (it shipped a `security` release-note fragment), so an upgrade is urgent

daemons.description: --check: what the running tw up on this machine reports; null when none runs here

whoami.description: who this CLI acts as and what that identity may do (GET /v1/whoami)

linked.description: through tw link (WhoIs); false: this machine's tw up

tenant.description: the default tenant; null when this identity can't list tenants (not an admin) or there is none

caps.description: the github.com/rosskukulinski/tailworks/cap/* capabilities held toward mgmt

console.description: the admin console URL this identity may open (<endpoint>/ui/, or <endpoint>/ui/approvals for an approver who isn't an admin); only through tw link, not --tsnet

approve.description: may decide Workflow approvals (github.com/rosskukulinski/tailworks/cap/approve); null when mgmt is too old to say

mcpTools.description: the MCP tools mgmt's /mcp allows; null when mgmt is too old to say

tenantAdmin.description: tenant admin (github.com/rosskukulinski/tailworks/cap/tenant-admin): each valid grant value's tenants and actions; empty when none

invalidTenantAdmin.description: github.com/rosskukulinski/tailworks/cap/tenant-admin values that grant nothing, each with the reason

completion.description: tw completion <shell>: the script (without --json it is printed as is)

status.description: health of mgmt, the host(s), the tenant and deployments. On the host (no linked): supervisor, mgmt, host, workloads, objectsByStatus, ...; on a linked machine (linked present): linked, whoami, hosts and tenants[].deployments

linked.description: the tw link this machine uses; present only on a linked machine, and it selects that field set

whoami.description: linked machine: mgmt's GET /v1/whoami answer as is (not the tw whoami result)

hosts.description: linked machine: every host mgmt knows

warmKeys.description: the operator tenant's pooled preauthorized join keys in mgmt custody (per tenant: tenants[].warmKeys); tw down revokes them

workerInternet.description: this host's Worker internet egress (tw up --worker-internet): what the running host reports, else tw.json's

tenants.description: each tenant this machine serves; on a linked machine each has deployments (the latest per workload)

unsafeFlags.description: host: the unsafe tw up flags saved in tw.json and re-applied on every tw up (insecure-shared-host, allow-experimental-flags, local-dev); [] when none

containers.description: host: this host's containers (Go field names)

hostCapacity.description: every host's container capacity and usage

degradedStores.description: stores whose replay stopped at a journal entry they can't apply; absent when none

items.description: the host's workloads as tw-hostd reports them (Go field names: TenantID, Workload, DeploymentID, Status, Error, ...)

unsafeFlags.description: the unsafe tw up flags saved in tw.json and re-applied on every later tw up (insecure-shared-host, allow-experimental-flags, local-dev); [] when none

uninstall.description: tw uninstall: the plan (with --dry-run) or what it did

console.description: the admin console URL (<endpoint>/ui/); omitted under --tsnet

tenant set.description: the tenant after the update (the /v1 Tenant)

types.description: tw types: the declaration file written (or with --check, compared)

changed.description: the file was written (or, with --check, would be: then the command fails with types_stale)

dev.description: tw dev --once (the smoke test); without --once, see dev.event

serves.description: url plus the MCP route for an MCP app

callers.description: tw dev --caller: one extra identity each, with its own local URL

as.description: the login of an untagged caller

dev.event.description: tw dev --json without --once: one per line on stdout. ready (first, with url, serves, workload, node, as, tags), inspector (with --inspector-port: addr, ws), console (url of the read-only data console, unless --console-port -1), then reload or error on each change, request (record) for each request the app serves, stopping on Ctrl-C

callers.description: tw dev --caller: one extra identity each, with its own local URL

as.description: the login of an untagged caller

deployImage.description: one image of a container class, pinned by mgmt at deploy (ADR-032 D3): hosts pull repository@digest

name.description: the class's wrangler images key (absent: the default image)

ref.description: the image as the bundle names it

from.description: what ref resolved through: "alias <target>", "public <ref>", or the upstream ref and its digest

deploy.description: the result, on stdout; progress is deploy.event lines on stderr

public.description: the public URL and state, if the app has public routes

images.description: container classes: what each image was pinned to

warnings.description: wrangler config tailworks ignores, one line per key

preview.description: --preview: the preview's own workload name (<workload>--preview-<alias>); workload is the workload it previews

policyApplied.description: --apply-policy: what mgmt wrote to the tailnet policy before the deploy (as tw policy --apply's applied)

deploy.event.description: tw deploy --json: one per line on stderr: start, preflight, policy (--apply-policy), build, log (container image builds), placed, status (each change), ready, then public_wait and public with --wait-public. A failure ends with an error line ({"error": ...}) instead. tw rollback --json prints the same lines without build, log and public

images.description: ready: the container images' pins, as the result's images

deploymentRecord.description: one entry of a workload's deployment history (the /v1 DeploymentRecord, ADR-046)

status.description: the current deployment's status (assigned, starting, active, failed); older ones are superseded or stopped

hostStatus.description: the host's last report, kept after the deployment is superseded: active means it was serving

bundleSHA256.description: hex SHA-256 of the bundle; empty for a deployment without one

bundleRetained.description: false once retention pruned the bundle: it can no longer be rolled back to

rollbackOf.description: set on a rollback: the deployment whose bundle it redeployed

deployments.description: tw deployments <workload>: its history, newest first

bundleRetention.description: how many of the newest bundles per workload mgmt keeps (0 = every bundle)

rollback.description: the result, on stdout; progress is deploy.event lines on stderr (start, preflight, placed, status, ready)

rollbackOf.description: the deployment whose bundle was redeployed

promote.description: the result, on stdout; progress is deploy.event lines on stderr (start, preflight, placed, status, ready)

promotedFrom.description: the preview deployment whose bundle was deployed

truncated.description: More objects matched than the ceiling (--limit, default 5000) let through.

expose names.description: the public names the tenant owns (ADR-029)

secret bulk.description: the names set, in input order; never values (a failure is an error naming set, failed and not attempted)

kvKey.description: a Workers KV key as list() returns it

namespace.description: the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)
the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)
the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)
the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)

kv key get.description: the value base64-encoded (without --json, the raw bytes on stdout)

namespace.description: the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)
the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)

kv key list.description: names, expirations and metadata; never values

namespace.description: the KV namespace (its kv_namespaces id, or the binding name)

queueInfo.description: a tenant queue and its counters (ADR-039)

backlog.description: messages kept: in flight and delayed included

oldestAt.description: unix ms of the oldest message

queueMessage.description: a queue message as peeked (body base64)

approvalWait.description: One approval wait of one Workflow instance (docs/approvals.md; mgmt's Approval).

approvals.description: tw approvals: what waits for a decision (with --all, decided ones too).

approve.description: tw approve: the approval as decided, with the approver's verified identity.

notify.description: tw notify [show], set, test and rm: the tenant's notification webhook (only its origin and header names are shown; test adds the delivery outcome; rm prints only tenantID)

logs.line.description: tw logs --json for raw output (--console, --component, or a workload without request records): one per log line on stdout (with -f, until stopped)

host.description: the replica's host (from a linked machine)

logs.record.description: tw logs <workload> --json (the default, without --console): one structured request record per line on stdout (ADR-045)

doctor.description: printed also when a check fails; then doctor_failed follows on stderr

group.description: the section the human output lists the check under: Install, Tailnet, Storage, Isolation, Linux host or Other

host add.description: the join key is written to joinFile (0600), never printed

tiers.description: what the host offers: its isolation tiers (process, microvm) and containers

arch.description: the host's GOARCH (amd64, arm64); absent for a host that never reported it

features.description: host features it offers (kv, r2, d1, telemetry, ...)

backup.description: tw backup: the new backup directory and its backup.json

restore.description: tw restore: what was restored, where the replaced state was kept, and the restore generation after the fence (SQLite stores)

custody migrate.description: tw custody migrate: every file custody entry mapped to its name, copied to setec and read back (--dry-run: what would be copied), the names indexed in custody_names, the state kept before tw.json was switched

upgrade.description: tw upgrade: on a tw up machine {plan, upgraded, backup?, rolledBack?, health?, notActiveBefore?, agentSkills?}; tw upgrade fleet (or tw upgrade on a linked machine): the plan (--plan: {from, to, steps, breaking, blockers, warnings}) or the upgrade run {id, to, state, steps}; tw upgrade fleet status|pause|resume|abort print the run ({runs: []} when there is none).

notActiveBefore.description: deployments that weren't active before the upgrade; the health check didn't count them

agentSkills.description: what the new tw's agent setup --refresh did to the user-scope agent skills tw wrote

upgrade rollback.description: tw upgrade rollback: the release it went back from and to, whether the store went back too (mode restore: the backup restored, the restore generation after the fence on SQLite), the state kept before the rollback, and what is left to do by hand (a Postgres store)

host vmcheck.description: a microVM's report (workload, pid, rssKB, stats, fsbench, keyscan); with --container, Go field names (Workload, Class, Object, PID, RSSKB, KeyScan)

ref.description: pass it to tw docs show
